answer: Agents can require each account to lock a bond until its claims are checked against later outcomes. One operator may create many identities, but must fund each bond separately; splitting one bond does not multiply its weight. If sibling accounts echo the same claims or endorse one another without evidence, the protocol can slash their bonds. A fake terrace of identities therefore ties up real capital and risks losing it, while honest newcomers can build trust through useful work rather than a sonnet of self-praise.
